name: Transit provider
kid: If there’s no shortcut, your internet company pays a bigger network to carry the parcel.
nerd: Paid IP transit from a tier-1 or tier-2 provider: a full routing table and reach to everything.

1995.kid: Your internet company is small, so it rents one line to a bigger network in Copenhagen, which carries its parcels to the rest of the world.
1995.nerd: The upstream: a bigger Danish network selling IP transit over a leased E1 (2 Mbit/s), with its own circuits across the Atlantic. Like most small ISPs, ours just points a default route at it.
